compile.detail:
**yolov8n.onnx → yolov8n.fp32.plan**  ·  TensorRT 10.3.0

The engine is on disk and this is the file that gets deployed. Nothing has been run yet, so none of this is a speed measurement — the build time above is how long it took to CREATE, not how fast it goes.

**Built at FP32, and every layer stayed there.** Nothing fell back.

**Layout conversion — 23% of layers**

57 of 248 layers do no maths. They only rearrange data so the next layer can read it.

Around 8% is normal at FP32. What this number is really for is comparing two builds of the SAME model: a jump after a precision change is the cost of extra shuffling, not a worse choice of kernel. At 23% a large share of this engine is moving data rather than computing — worth comparing against another precision before concluding the model is simply expensive.

**What the engine is made of**

| Kind | Count | What it does |
|---|---:|---|
| PointWiseV2 | 69 | elementwise maths, fused |
| CaskConvolution | 61 | convolutions |
| Reformat | 57 | layout/precision conversion — overhead, not maths |
| NoOp | 23 | removed entirely |
| Constant | 15 | — |
| Slice | 9 | slicing |
| Fill | 6 | — |
| CaskPooling | 3 | — |
| Resize | 2 | resizing |
| Shuffle | 2 | reshapes and transposes |
| CaskSoftMaxV2 | 1 | — |

These are TensorRT's own kernel families, after it merged what it could — which is why the count does not match the ONNX node count.
warnings: This model has dynamic input shapes. The engine was built for images=(1, 3, 480, 640) — pass shape_profile to benchmark a different shape.
First build on this GPU, so every kernel had to be timed (5s). The timings are now cached; rebuilding this model after surgery or quantization will be far quicker.
